newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan non-banks' lending down 4.4 pct at end-March.
newsitem.headline: Japan non-banks' lending down 4.4 pct at end-March.

text.p: Outstanding loans by Japan's 249 non-bank financial institutions at the end of March this year fell 4.4 percent from a year earlier to 50.74 trillion yen, the Finance Ministry said on Monday.
Lending to companies amounted to 40.40 trillion yen, down 7.5 percent, while loans to individuals rose 10.0 percent to 10.34 trillion yen, the ministry said.
In Japan, companies in the business of property-related financing are classified as non-bank financial institutions.

As in the case of seven failed Japanese housing loan firms, or "jusen", non-banks have been hit by sharp falls in property prices since the bursting of Japan's 1980s "bubble economy" of inflated land and asset prices.
